why: Asks what the clause does, and 'both parties released by an extraordinary event' follows once the concept is grasped; the other options are named by their own clauses.
Asks for the heading a clause is filed under — a drafting-convention label rather than a concept.
The ongoing monitoring-and-enforcement role follows from what managing a service level means.
Matching a description to one of four procurement acronyms; the distinction between them is a naming convention.
Which heading of a particular model contract template these clauses sit under is arbitrary, and the bank concedes another option is equally defensible.
Follows from only the contract documents being enforceable; scenario reasoning throughout.
The dependence-at-renewal argument is reasoned from what happens when ownership is unstated.
The continuity problem escrow solves follows from the vendor holding the only copy of the code.
Change control follows from needing to re-baseline scope, cost and schedule together.
Follows from a percentage being unenforceable until measurement and exclusions are agreed.
Reasoning from support lifecycles being shorter than the contract term.
The 'risk to the party best able to manage it' principle follows from what mispriced risk does to a bid.
Follows from outsourcing delivery not outsourcing the state's obligation to the citizen.
The pre-agreed nature of the sum is spelled out in the option, so the concept rather than the legal label decides it.
The lock-in and continuity argument is reasoned from what a handover must achieve.
